claim.claim-text: 1. An implantable device for controllably applying a neural stimulus, the device comprising:
2. The implantable device of claim 1 wherein the control unit is configured to produce the estimation P' from an empirical relationship of stimulus current to measured ECAP amplitude.

3. The implantable device of claim 1 wherein the control unit is configured to determine the estimation P' as P' = (V+K)/I, where V is ECAP amplitude, K is a constant or function which relates P to a stimulus threshold T, and I is stimulus current amplitude.
4. The implantable device of claim 1 wherein the control unit is configured to scale an error signal of the feedback loop by 1/P'.

5. The implantable device of any one of claims 1 to 4 wherein the control unit is configured to adaptively compensate for changes in the feedback loop by maintaining a corner frequency of the feedback loop at a desired value or within a desired range.

6. The implantable device of claim 5 wherein the desired value or range of the corner frequency is selected to suitably attenuate low frequency noise such as heartbeat as well as high frequency noise such as electrical amplifier noise.
7. A non-transitory computer readable medium for controllably applying a neural stimulus, comprising the following instructions for execution by one or more processors:

8. The non-transitory computer readable medium of claim 7 further comprising computer program code means for producing the estimation P' from an empirical relationship of stimulus current to measured ECAP amplitude.

9. The non-transitory computer readable medium of claim 7 further comprising computer program code means for determining the estimation P' as P' = (V+K)/I, where V is ECAP amplitude, K is a constant or function which relates P to a stimulus threshold T, and I is stimulus current amplitude.
10. The non-transitory computer readable medium of claim 7 further comprising computer program code means for scaling an error signal of the feedback loop by 1/P'.

11. The non-transitory computer readable medium of any one of claims 7 to 10 further comprising computer program code means for adaptively compensating for changes in the feedback loop by maintaining a corner frequency of the feedback loop at a desired value or within a desired range.

12. The non-transitory computer readable medium of claim 11 wherein the desired value or range of the corner frequency is selected to suitably attenuate low frequency noise such as heartbeat as well as high frequency noise such as electrical amplifier noise.
